what_it_does: Some researchers want to perform logic operations (AND, OR, NOT, and combinations thereof) directly inside a memory chip rather than shuttling data to a separate processor — a concept called in-memory computing. This paper uses a type of non-volatile memory called RRAM (Resistive RAM), where each storage cell is a tiny resistor whose resistance can be switched between high and low, representing 0 and 1. The cell pairs a transistor with one RRAM element (called a 1T1R structure). A 4-to-1 multiplexer (a circuit that selects one of four input signals to pass through) is a standard building block in digital logic. Existing designs needed 10 sequential steps to perform this selection inside the RRAM array; the authors redesign it using NAND logic patterns that complete the same operation in only 3 steps, cutting the time by 75%. The same idea extends to addition, subtraction, and comparison circuits.
